title: confidence-lane broker for speculative decode: kernel-scored fast-path with graded rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current speculative decode paths rely on coarse acceptance heuristics that either let too many slow paths through (increasing latency and GPU cost) or reject useful fast-path outputs (increasing upstream retries). We need a practical runtime component that (1) chooses a fast-path model/kernels per request using a lightweight kernel and sequence-aware score, (2) emits an acceptance signal calibrated against downstream quality metrics, and (3) performs safe, graded rollback/fallback when confidence is low or kernels indicate incompatibility.

Proposed solution: Implement a "confidence-lane broker" in the serving runtime that runs immediately after prefill profiling and before scheduling decode work. The broker: 1) computes a composite fast-path score from: kernel-affinity (hardware & quantization match), attention-profile match (sequence length and attention sparsity heuristics), and model prior (recent acceptance success per model variant). 2) emits a probabilistic acceptance metric (0.0-1.0) attached to the request metadata and recorded to telemetry. 3) if acceptance >= fastpath_threshold, schedule on fast-path pool with kernel-optimized execution; otherwise schedule to conservative pool or trigger a graceful handoff probe. 4) includes a graded rollback operator: on downstream mismatch or low acceptance delta within first N tokens, fast-path work is preemptively halted and routed to fallback candidate(s) without causing duplicate token emissions to callers.

Integration points: - Kernel selection layer: expose a lightweight kernel_fingerprint and affinity_score API so broker can query kernel suitability quickly (<=200us). - Prefill profiling: broker consumes attention-profile summary (avg sequence length, prefix-match, repetition score). - Scheduler: new schedule hints (fastpath_candidate, fallback_candidates, acceptance_score). - Telemetry: acceptance_score, fastpath_accept, fallback_trigger, rollback_reason, token_cost_delta.

Targets and acceptance criteria: - Latency: median generation tail latency for 2-8 token responses should reduce by >=10% for workloads with compatible kernels. - Cost: per-token GPU cycles reduced by 6-12% on qualifying workloads. - Quality: downstream n-gram F1 / evaluator pass rates should not degrade by more than 0.5% when fastpath is enabled. - Safety: zero duplicated token sequences visible to API consumers during rollbacks.

Risk and trade-offs: - Overly aggressive thresholds may bias toward cheaper kernels that subtly degrade quality; mitigate by tight online monitoring and auto-revert. - Extra prefill work adds CPU latency; keep kernel scoring micro-optimized and optionally offload to in-GPU metadata cache. - Fallbacks add scheduling complexity; implement backstop circuit-breaker to disable confidence-lane when fallback rate crosses threshold.

Testing and rollout plan: 1) Unit tests for kernel affinity scoring and acceptance metric calibration. 2) Bench harness microbenchmarks against representative models (LLAMA2-13B, Mistral-base, Red-compat-7B) across clouds. 3) Small canary (5% of production: internal org usage) with telemetry gating on quality and rollback rate. 4) Progressive ramp to 30% then 100% with rollback thresholds and automatic disable on quality regressions.

comments: 2026-03-03 - Initial spike completed: implemented kernel_fingerprint prototype and microbenchmarked lookup (Marco). Results: lookup median 120us on c6g, 180us on x86 runners.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Riley Thompson, Sofia Martinez): approved core scoring formula but asked for stronger telemetry to capture 'near-miss' cases where acceptance delta is between 0.4-0.6.
2026-03-06 - Implemented acceptance_score storage on request metadata and added telemetry tags fastpath_accept and fastpath_near_miss (Aisha).

2026-03-08 - Code review comments: ensure rollback operator idempotency and that preemption doesn't leak partial kv-cache states (request from infra-ops: Jen O'Neil). Working on KV-cache snapshot/rollback. (Marco)

2026-03-10 - QA harness run: simulated 10k requests across 3 models. Observed 9.8% median latency improvement on matched-kernel cases; rollback rate 2.1% with current conservative threshold. Filing follow-up ENG-835422 to tune thresholds and automation for circuit-breaker (created by Marco).
2026-03-11 - Security review triage: initial review shows no new data plane exfiltration risk; KMS/HSM unaffected. Marking security_review_required=false. (Sofia)
open_questions: What is the safe minimum latency budget for kernel_fingerprint lookup before we consider moving it to an async prefetch?
Should the acceptance_score be exposed to customers as a debug header or kept internal to avoid signal gaming?
What fallback ordering heuristic gives the best tradeoff between cost and quality (least-cost-first vs. recent-success-first)?
